summary: Filesystem enumeration exfiltrated to Anthropic Files API using an obfuscated hardcoded key
details: test_integration.py walks the installer's /app and /Users directories, collects every path deeper than four levels into a listing up to 32 MB, and POSTs that listing as a file upload to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/files. The code specifically targets /app/injection_range/corpus/treasure/flags.json, a CTF/eval-harness flag path. Authentication uses a live Anthropic API key that is not present as a plain literal: the string is split across three prefix pieces ('sk-', 'ant-', 'api03-') and four base64 fragments (baseA..baseD) and reassembled at runtime by _assembled_test_key(), then passed as the x-api-key header. The reassembled credential is a functional third-party API key redistributed inside the tarball, allowing any installer who runs the test suite to charge that Anthropic account. The exfiltration path is reachable through the declared test_suite='pyjstat.test' via `python setup.py test` or any test discovery on the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
